div.head: V As 1.1
div.ab: Gif se hlaford ðonne wille ðone mon mid woh fordón, berecce hine ðonne, gif he mæge, on folcgemote; gif he laþleas sy, sæte hwylcne hlaforde on þa gewitnysse swelcne he þonne wille; forþon ic wille, þæt ylc þæra þe laþleas beo, folgige swylcum hlaforde swylce he ðonne wylle.

Gif se hlaford þonne wille ðone man mid wo(h) fordon, berecce hine þonne, gif he mage, on folcgemote; ⁊ gif he ladleas beo, sece swylcne hlaford on þa gewitnesse swylcne he wille; forðy þe ic an, ðæt ælc ðara þe ladleas beo, folgie swilcum hlaforde swylcum he wille.

Si tunc dominus uelit eum disfacere, disracionet se, si possit, in conuentu publico; et si culpa careat, perquirat sibi dominum in testimonio quem uoluerit; quia concedo, ut omnis qui innocens sit seruiat domino cui uelit.

Gif se hlaford þonne wille ðone man mid woh fordon, berecce hine þonne, gif he mage, on folcgemote; ⁊ gif he laþleas beo, sece swylcne halford on þa gewitnesse swylcne he wille; forðy þe ic an, ðæt ælc ðara þe laþleas beo, folgie swilcum hlaforde swylcum he wille.

If, however, the lord wrongfully intends to ruin the man, he [the man] shall clear himself, if he can, in a public meeting. If he proves himself free from crime, he may seek, with the witness of those present, any lord he wishes; for I give permission to everyone who is free from crime to serve any lord he may wish.

If the lord, however, wishes wrongfully to ruin the man, he is then to justify himself, if he can, in a public meeting; and if he is innocent, he is to seek such lord as he will in the witness of that meeting, because I grant that each of those who are innocent may serve such lord as he wishes.

Wenn jener [erste] Herr den Mann dagegen unrechtmässig verderben will, so reinige sich dieser dann im Volksgericht, wenn er kann; und wenn er [hierdurch] schuldlos sich erweist, so suche er kraft dieser Zeugenschaft solchen Herrn, wie er (dann Ld) will; denn ich erlaube (will Ld), dass jeder, wer schuldlos ist, sich einem solchen Herrn, dem er (dann Ld) will, unterordne.

If, on the other hand, that [first] lord wishes to ruin the man unlawfully, let the man then clear himself in the public court if he can; and if he proves himself guiltless [by this], let him seek, by virtue of this testimony, such a lord as he (then, Ld) wishes; for I grant (will, Ld) that everyone who is guiltless may submit himself to such a lord as he (then, Ld) wishes.
